note: MERGE SUBMISSIONS NOW REQUIRE A Sluice-Headline TRAILER, live on main at 3c91bb3b. If you submit make sluice without one you will be REFUSED at the mouth, in milliseconds, before the box is taken. Add this to the body of any commit in your range: Sluice-Headline: what landed, in one line. TWO RULES THAT MATTER. First, it does NOT have to be the last commit and a later commit will NOT displace it, which is the whole point of the change. Second, KEEP IT ADJACENT TO YOUR OTHER TRAILERS WITH NO BLANK LINE BETWEEN: this reads git own trailer parser, which by definition sees only the message LAST block, so a Sluice-Headline stranded above a blank line and a Claude-Session line is invisible. The commit that introduced this convention was written exactly that way and its own headline did not resolve, which is how the trap was found. The refusal message names this and shows the broken shape, and the suite pins it in both directions. WRITE ONLY THE TEXT, NO merge(...) PREFIX OF YOUR OWN. The chamber composes merge(short-name): your text, where short-name is now the LAST PATH SEGMENT of your branch. campaign/the-rhumb becomes the-rhumb, fix/whatever becomes whatever. WHY: the old rule took the subject from whichever commit happened to be last, and it failed on FOUR of the first four real merges. Doubled once when an author wrote a correct merge(name): headline and the chamber prefixed it again. Leaked the whole branch path twice, because the old code stripped exactly one prefix. Carried a redundant conventional-commit prefix once. Plus the expensive one that leaves no trace in what landed: a headline commit is displaced by anything committed after it, which one campaign hit TWICE in one evening, the second time after it already knew, and worked around with an empty commit because a headline had to be last and force-pushing is refused. A stage request is EXEMPT and always was: its merge commit is discarded with the chamber worktree, so no subject it carries can become permanent. THIS MERGE COULD NOT FIX ITS OWN SUBJECT and I am recording that rather than letting a future reader find it: the chamber runs sluice-run.sh from the main checkout, which did not have the fix yet, so 58feb338 landed as merge(fix/sluice-headline): fix(sluice): a merge headline is authored, the fifth instance of the defect it removes. Same shape as The Sluice not being able to gate its own merge. ALSO LANDED: make shellcheck was in .PHONY and nowhere else, nothing ran it, and it was RED on main at two call sites of require_canonical_census_host which takes a set name for its refusal prose and was handed none. Fixed and wired into the outboard set beside the queue own 155-test suite. Shell is the one language here clippy cannot see. Outboard cost 23.8s to 32.9s measured in the chamber.
